html_source: Molly is appalled at the memory of taking care of Bloom’s cut, signifying that she lacks a motherly instinct. This contrasts with Penelope’s characterization, where she was praised for raising her son, Telemachus, alone while Odysseus was away for several years. Not to mention, later on in the chapter Molly wonders why Milly only sent her a card, but sent Bloom a longer, more tender letter. This demonstrates that she doesn’t have a bond with her child as much as Penelope did with Telemachus.
